head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Configuration
The characteristics and documents used to describe a specific product state.
A unit is described by its fitted replaceable module and software release.
Configuration management (CM)
An organized way to identify product states, review changes, maintain records and verify agreement.
A team can reconstruct what changed on a controller.
Configuration item (CI)
A part, assembly or software component managed separately because its changes matter.
The controller program has its own revision record.
Configuration management plan (CMP)
A project-specific description of control rules, owners and decision paths.
A plan names who approves software changes.
Equipment breakdown structure (EBS)
A hierarchy of system elements and their parent-child relationships.
A replaceable module appears under the water-handling assembly.
Work breakdown structure (WBS)
A hierarchy of tasks or deliverables needed to carry out a project.
Testing a prototype is project work.
Unique identifier
A code that points to one intended record or object.
An individual controller has serial 0057.
Part number
An identifier for a component design or type.
Replaceable module-02 identifies one replaceable module design.
Serial number
A code that distinguishes one physical unit from others of the same type.
A particular replaceable module has a unique serial.
Revision
A controlled version of a document, design or software item.
Drawing R4 replaces R3 for a later release.
Baseline
An agreed reference description that is changed through a defined decision.
Version R4 is accepted for the next build.
Functional baseline (FBL)
A reference for required overall behavior and interfaces.
The unit must perform an agreed operating cycle.
Allocated baseline (ABL)
A reference assigning requirements to selected lower-level elements.
Timing behavior is assigned to the controller.
Product baseline (PBL)
A detailed accepted description for making and supporting a specific product version.
Released records specify the board and cable types.
Technical data package (TDP)
A coordinated collection of product descriptions and related instructions.
Drawings, parts lists and test methods form a package.
Technical data management (TDM)
Controlling the versions, release and accessibility of technical information.
An obsolete assembly drawing is marked superseded.
Change request
A documented proposal to alter an accepted item or its description.
A team requests a different replaceable module connector.
Engineering change proposal (ECP)
A structured technical change request with a reason, scope and impact assessment.
A request explains a replaceable module substitution and its effects.
Configuration control
The review, decision and release process for changes to controlled descriptions.
The accepted program revision follows a formal decision.
Configuration Control Board (CCB)
A designated group that evaluates changes within assigned authority.
A cross-functional group considers a new motor option.
Decision authority
The role or group permitted to accept or refuse a given change.
A technical lead may approve a minor documentation change.
Interface
A point where components or functions must work together.
A cable plug meets a controller socket.
Deviation
A documented permission to depart from a requirement in a defined case.
One trial unit is allowed a different bracket.
Waiver
Formal acceptance of a specified nonconformance under the applicable rules.
An owner accepts an identified cosmetic defect.
Configuration status accounting (CSA)
Records that connect item identities, changes, decisions and implementation state.
The register shows which units use device software 2.3.
As-built record
Evidence describing what was actually produced or installed.
A build record lists the electronics module revision.
Configuration audit
A structured comparison of claims, evidence and the item being reviewed.
Reviewers inspect records and a completed device.
Functional Configuration Audit (FCA)
A review of whether evidence supports required behavior.
Timing tests support the operation requirement.
Physical Configuration Audit (PCA)
A review of whether the actual product matches its accepted detailed description.
The fitted board is checked against a parts record.
Action item
An assigned follow-up task with an expected result and tracked status.
A technician must confirm a missing software label.
Implementation status
The recorded stage of authorized work on a particular item or release.
An accepted change may still await installation.
Integrated logistics support (ILS)
Work to ensure a product can be operated and supported over time.
Training and spare-parts changes accompany a new replaceable module.
